newsitem.title: HUNGARY: RESEARCH ALERT-Merrill rates OTP "long term reduce".
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Merrill rates OTP "long term reduce".

text.p: Hungary's largest commercial bank OTP remains overvalued compared with Poland's regional banks, Merrill Lynch said on Thursday, maintaining its "long term reduce" rating for the stock.

Merrill Lynch said in a report, dated August 11, that it forecast a P/E ratio of 11.6 for OTP for 1998 and a price per net asset value (P/NAV) ratio of 2.8, against the Polish regional banks' respective averages of 6.4 and 1.3.
OTP's P/E was 19.3 in 1996, while the P/NAV was four.
Merrill Lynch added that OTP's balance sheet was likely to see weak growth, by 17 percent in 1997 and 15 percent in 1998.

Group loans are unlikely to grow more than a nominal eight percent in 1997 and 13 percent in 1998, while deposits will probably rise by 17 percent this year and 15 percent next year, mainly driven by OTP's success with retail current accounts, Merrill Lynch said.

The group is likely to contain operating cost growth to a rate below revenue growth, leding to a modest decline in the consolidated cost/income ratio from 78 percent in 1996 and to 76 percent by 1998, it added.
Merrill said that OTP's consolidated net profit was likely to rise to 13 billion forints in 1997 and to 16.74 billion in 1998 from 10.09 billion in 1996.
